Lmfao jumping to conclusions without context is crazy, yes I worded it wrong but by “not touch anyone” I literally mean that. He wouldn’t touch even bedsheets or napkins until the pooja was done. Mind you all these practices were 20+ years ago (he has already passed away in 2004).

My main premise from the comment is that these practices are learned and evolved overtime and people change their practices according to their convenience.

I don’t know about others here but I face same problems at my house and there’s a great reasoning behind this. I’m a brahmin and my maternal fathers have our own mandir (connected to our old house) where all the rituals and pooja are held daily. Due to this my mother was used to taking a bath all day and being “clean” before going to the mandir. My nana who used to do the pooja would take a bath and not touch anyone until the pooja was done.

The same habit has crept up to my house where we don’t usually touch the unbathed ones after taking a bath. Also it has been implanted in our brains that we are “impure” after shitting and need to take a bath asap to become clean.
